title_en: Wang Yongsheng v. Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nanjing Hexi Branch — dispute over savings deposit contract
ruling_gist_en: Where a criminal takes advantage of a commercial bank's neglect in the management and maintenance of its self-service teller machines, by installing a card reader at the card swiping slot at the entrance of a self-service banking outlet and installing a camera device on the upper part of the teller machine, thereby窃取 a depositor's debit card number, information, and password, duplicating a counterfeit debit card, and withdrawing or spending money from the depositor's debit card account, it shall be determined that the commercial bank has failed to provide a necessary safe and confidential environment for depositors conducting transactions at its self-service teller machines, constituting a breach of contract. Where a depositor files a lawsuit requesting the commercial bank to assume payment liability under the savings deposit contract, and the commercial bank defends on the ground that the shortage of funds in the depositor's debit card account was caused by criminal conduct and that it should not bear civil liability, the people's court shall not support such defense.

full_text_en:
Wang Yongsheng v. Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nanjing Hexi Sub-branch — Dispute over Savings Deposit Contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a criminal takes advantage of a commercial bank's negligence in the management and maintenance of its self-service ATM to steal the card number, information and password of a depositor's debit card by installing a card reader at the card-swiping slot at the entrance of a self-service banking outlet and a camera device on the upper part of the ATM, then reproduces a counterfeit debit card and withdraws or consumes money from the depositor's debit card account, it shall be determined that the commercial bank has failed to provide a necessary safe and confidential environment for depositors conducting transactions at its self-service ATM, constituting a breach of contract. If the depositor files a lawsuit requesting the commercial bank to assume the obligation of payment in accordance with the savings deposit contract, and the commercial bank defends on the ground that the shortage of funds in the depositor's debit card is caused by criminal acts and it should not bear civil liability, the people's court shall not support such defense.

Plaintiff: Wang Yongsheng, male, 36 years old, Han ethnicity, manager of Jiangsu Tianmu Construction Group Co., Ltd., residing at Yagui Garden, Gulou District, Nanjing.

Defendant: Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nanjing Hexi Sub-branch, domiciled at Caochangmen Street, Gulou District, Nanjing.

Person in charge: Pang Nanning, sub-branch president.

The plaintiff, Wang Yongsheng, filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province against the defendant, Bank of China Co., Ltd., Nanjing Hexi Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China), over a dispute over a savings deposit contract.

The plaintiff Wang Yongsheng alleged: On October 9, 2007, the plaintiff obtained a Bank of China debit card (card No. 6013821200011990595) from the defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China. On the evening of December 2, 2007, the plaintiff withdrew RMB 5,000 from a self-service ATM at the Self-Service Banking Outlet of the Xiaguan Rehenan Road Sub-branch of Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Rehenan Road Sub-branch of Bank of China), and inquired that the deposit balance was RMB 463,942.2. On the afternoon of December 5, 2007, when the plaintiff was about to withdraw RMB 10,000 at the Jiangning Sub-branch of Bank of China, the counter clerk informed him that the balance in the card was only over RMB 2,800. That evening, the plaintiff inquired again and found that another RMB 2,000 had been reduced from the card. The plaintiff immediately reported the case to the Gulou Branch of Nanjing Public Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Gulou Public Security Branch). Upon investigation by the public security authorities, it was found that three men had installed a storage-type card reading device on the automatic door of the Self-Service Banking Outlet of the Rehenan Road Sub-branch of Bank of China and installed a probe on the ATM, thereby obtaining the password and information of the plaintiff's debit card, then reproduced two counterfeit cards and withdrew or consumed RMB 463,942.2 in Beijing, Jiangxi and other places. Later, one of the criminals, Tang Hairen, a person not involved in this case, was captured by the public security authorities and was convicted of credit card fraud by the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing in Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu刑Chu Zi, sentenced to ten years and six months' imprisonment and fined RMB 100,000. This criminal judgment has taken legal effect. After the above incident occurred, the plaintiff repeatedly negotiated with the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China). On January 24, 2008, the plaintiff and the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China reached an agreement whereby the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China first lent the plaintiff RMB 232,000 to pay some migrant workers' wages, and the issue would be further resolved after the matter was clarified. There exists a savings deposit contract between the plaintiff and the defendant, and the defendant has an obligation to protect the security of the plaintiff's funds. Due to deficiencies in the security management of its self-service ATM, the defendant left an opportunity for criminals to exploit, resulting in the plaintiff's deposit of RMB 463,942.2 in the card being withdrawn or consumed by criminals using counterfeit debit cards, and the plaintiff was not at fault. The plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to pay the plaintiff RMB 463,942.2 in deposit in accordance with the savings deposit contract signed by both parties, as well as interest on the above amount from December 4, 2007 to the date of actual payment.

The plaintiff Wang Yongsheng provided the following evidence:

1. One copy of Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu刑Chu Zi of the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, to prove that the criminal Tang Hairen was lawfully sentenced to ten years and six months' imprisonment and fined RMB 100,000 for the crime of credit card fraud;

2. One copy of transaction list for debit card No. 6013821200011990595, to prove the transaction status of the debit card account involved in the case;

3. One copy of the agreement reached between the plaintiff and the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China on January 24, 2008, to prove that the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China first lent the plaintiff RMB 232,000 to pay migrant workers' wages.

The defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China argued: First, the Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu刑Chu Zi of the Gulou District People's Court confirmed that the criminal amount was RMB 428,709.50, and did not identify the 14 withdrawals totaling RMB 35,140 from the debit card account involved in the case in Beijing. It cannot be ruled out that the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng made these 14 withdrawals himself; the defendant only recognizes the criminal amount confirmed in the criminal judgment. Second, the shortage of funds in the plaintiff's debit card was caused by criminal acts, and the defendant should not bear civil liability for the loss of funds caused to the plaintiff by the criminal acts. In the process of providing services to the plaintiff, the defendant strictly complied with the relevant regulations of the regulatory authorities. The self-service banking outlets it established all had security prevention facilities that met the standards, and the defendant also reminded depositors to properly keep their debit card passwords through various means. The deposit in the plaintiff's debit card account was stolen because the plaintiff failed to properly keep the password, and the plaintiff himself was at fault. In summary, the defendant requested the court to make a judgment based on the facts found.

The defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China submitted the following evidence:

1. One copy of the Security Prevention Facility Certificate issued by the Nanjing Public Security Bureau on December 24, 2007, and the ATM operating instructions and ATM interface prompts displayed by Bank of China to depositors, to prove that the defendant fulfilled its obligation to protect the security of depositors' deposits;

2. One copy of the debit card business registration form (with attached management agreement and bylaws), to prove the specific circumstances under which the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng applied for the debit card, and the fact that the defendant reasonably reminded the cardholder that "the cardholder shall properly keep the password, and the risks and losses caused by password leakage shall be borne by the cardholder himself";

3. One copy each of the bank statement and transaction detail, to prove the transaction status of the debit card account involved in the case;

4. One copy of an application submitted by the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China to the People's Court, to prove that the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China agreed to offset the RMB 232,000 it lent to Wang Yongsheng as a loan from the defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China in this case.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing lawfully collected the following evidence:

1. Records of inquiries by the Gulou Public Security Branch of Tang Hairen, a person not involved in the case, and the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng, to prove that Tang Hairen and others obtained the information and password of the plaintiff's debit card by installing a card reader and an MP4 with a camera function, then reproduced two counterfeit cards to withdraw or consume money;

2. A transaction detail from the Beijing Tianyuan Gongyu Sub-branch of Bank of China, to prove that between 22:22:09 on December 3, 2007 and 0:33:53 on December 4, 2007, the debit card No. 6013821200011990595 made 14 withdrawals totaling RMB 35,000 at the self-service ATM managed by the Beijing Tianyuan Gongyu Sub-branch, with an off-site withdrawal fee of RMB 140 incurred.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing lawfully organized the examination of evidence. The defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China had no objection to the authenticity of evidence 1, 2 and 3 submitted by the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng, but argued that the above evidence was irrelevant to whether the defendant should bear civil liability. The plaintiff had no objection to the authenticity of evidence 1, 2, 3 and 4 submitted by the defendant, but argued that evidence 1 and 2 could not prove that the self-service banking transaction venue provided by Bank of China could ensure the security of depositors' funds. After examining the evidence, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing confirmed the authenticity of all evidence submitted by the plaintiff and the defendant.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing found through trial:

On October 9, 2007, the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng obtained one Great Wall Electronic Debit Card (hereinafter referred to as the debit card), card No. 6013821200011990595, from the defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China. The debit card was a passbook-less card. Wang Yongsheng signed the business registration form, on the back of which was attached a management agreement and debit card bylaws, stating "the cardholder shall properly keep the password, and the risks and losses caused by password leakage shall be borne by the cardholder himself."

On the evening of December 2, 2007, Tang Hairen and four other persons, not involved in this case, went to the self-service banking outlet of the Rehenan Road Sub-branch of Bank of China, installed a card reader at the card-swiping slot at the door, and installed an MP4 with a camera function on the upper part of the ATM. At 19:05 on the same day, the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng used the debit card to withdraw RMB 5,000 from the ATM at that self-service banking outlet. Tang Hairen and others thus stole the card number, information and password of the plaintiff's debit card, and reproduced two counterfeit bank cards based on this. On December 3, 2007, three of Tang Hairen and others went to Nanchang with one of the counterfeit cards, while the other two went to Beijing with the other counterfeit card, and carried out credit card fraud activities respectively.

On December 6, 2007, Wang Yongsheng discovered the shortage of deposit in his debit card, immediately went to the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China to print the transaction details and reported the case to the Gulou Public Security Branch. After filing the case, the Gulou Public Security Branch captured Tang Hairen, a person not involved in the case, on January 11, 2008, and placed him under criminal detention on the same day. On May 22, 2008, the Gulou District People's Procuratorate of Nanjing initiated a public prosecution against Tang Hairen for credit card fraud before the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing. The court found after trial that on December 4 and 5, 2007, Tang Hairen and others used the reproduced bank cards to swipe and withdraw funds in Nanchang, Yugan and other places, totaling RMB 428,709.50. Accordingly, on June 5, 2008, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing issued Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu刑Chu Zi, sentencing Tang Hairen to ten years and six months' imprisonment for the crime of credit card fraud, and fining him RMB 100,000. This criminal judgment has taken legal effect.

In addition, the inquiry details provided by Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China showed: On December 3, 2007, RMB 50,000 was withdrawn over the counter at the Jiangning Dashikou Sub-branch of Bank of China from the debit card No. 6013821200011990595, and at 19:58 on the same day, RMB 5,000 was withdrawn from the ATM at the Guanghua Road Self-Service Banking Outlet of Bank of China. The plaintiff Wang Yongsheng confirmed that he himself made these two withdrawals. The transaction details provided by the Beijing Tianyuan Gongyu Sub-branch of Bank of China on December 22, 2007, which were lawfully collected by the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, showed: Between 22:22:09 on December 3, 2007 and 0:33:53 on December 4, 2007, the debit card No. 6013821200011990595 made 14 withdrawals totaling RMB 35,000 at the self-service ATM managed by that sub-branch, with an off-site withdrawal fee of RMB 140 incurred. The RMB 35,140 involved in the above 14 transactions was not confirmed as the criminal amount of Tang Hairen, a person not involved in the case, in Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu刑Chu Zi.

On January 24, 2008, the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng and the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China entered into an agreement stipulating: The Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China would first lend the plaintiff RMB 232,000 to help the plaintiff solve the problem of paying migrant workers' wages; if the plaintiff initiated a civil lawsuit against the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China and the court ruled that the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China should compensate the plaintiff, then the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China would have the right to offset the loan under this agreement against its claim. On the date the agreement was signed, the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China paid the plaintiff RMB 232,000. During the trial of this case, the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China submitted an application agreeing that the RMB 232,000 it lent to the plaintiff would be offset as a loan from the defendant Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China in this case. On March 12, 2008, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Xiaguan District People's Court of Nanjing against the Xiaguan Sub-branch of Bank of China as the defendant. On April 30, 2008, the Xiaguan District People's Court of Nanjing ruled to suspend the trial of that case. On June 5, 2008, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing issued a criminal judgment on the credit card fraud case. Later, considering the issue of standing, the plaintiff withdrew the lawsuit from the Xiaguan District People's Court of Nanjing and filed this lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing against Hexi Sub-branch of Bank of China as the defendant.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing lawfully conducted mediation, but due to significant differences of opinion, the parties failed to reach a mediated settlement.

The defendant, Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch, argued that Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu Chu Zi of the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing confirmed the amount of the crime as RMB 42,870,950, and did not recognize the RMB 35,140 withdrawn from the involved debit card account in Beijing, thus the possibility that the plaintiff, Wang Yongsheng, withdrew that amount himself could not be excluded. The defendant only recognized the amount of the crime confirmed in the criminal judgment. In this regard, the court held: first, although the aforesaid RMB 35,140 was not confirmed as part of the criminal amount of the non-party Tang Hairen in Criminal Judgment No. 241 (2008) Gu Chu Zi, this does not prove the defendant's claim that the plaintiff withdrew it himself. Second, according to the interrogation record of the non-party Tang Hairen prepared by the Gulou Public Security Sub-bureau, Tang Hairen and others, after replicating the plaintiff's debit card on the evening of December 2, 2007, left Nanjing and went to Nanchang, Yugan, and Beijing in Jiangxi Province, among other places. This indicates that the RMB 5,000 withdrawn from the involved debit card account at the Zhonghe Nanjing Guanghua Road self-service teller machine at 19:58 on the evening of December 3, 2007, was not withdrawn by Tang Hairen or others using the replicated fake bank card. The plaintiff also admitted to the fact of withdrawing RMB 5,000 at the Guanghua Road self-service teller machine at 19:58 on December 3, 2007. This fact also proves that at around 8:00 p.m. on December 3, 2007, the plaintiff was still in the urban area of Nanjing. The transaction record provided by Zhonghe Beijing Tianyuan Gongyu Sub-branch shows that the aforesaid RMB 35,140 was withdrawn between 22:22:09 on December 3, 2007, and 0:33:53 on December 4, 2007. This time period is less than two and a half hours from the time the plaintiff withdrew money at the Guanghua Road self-service teller machine. In light of common sense, it would be impossible for the plaintiff to travel from Nanjing to Beijing to withdraw money within such a short time. Therefore, Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch cannot prove that the RMB 35,140 was withdrawn upon the plaintiff's instructions, and it shall still bear the liability for payment of RMB 35,140 to Wang Yongsheng.

Based on the fact that the funds in the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng's debit card were withdrawn and consumed by criminals, Zhonghe Xiaguan Sub-branch lent RMB 232,000 to the plaintiff on January 24, 2008. It now agrees to offset this amount as a loan made by Zhonghe Xiaguan Sub-branch against the liability of the defendant Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch in this case. This is consistent with the true intent of the agreement signed by both parties, and was recognized by both Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch and the plaintiff during the trial. This is hereby allowed.

In summary, the shortage of funds in the plaintiff Wang Yongsheng's debit card account was caused by the defendant Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch's failure to fulfill its security and confidentiality obligations. The plaintiff's claim for payment of the deposit and corresponding interest from Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch is supported, but the RMB 232,000 already lent by Zhonghe Xiaguan Sub-branch shall be deducted. Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment on November 26, 2008:

The defendant, Zhonghe Xihe Sub-branch, shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay the plaintiff, Wang Yongsheng, the deposit amount of RMB 231,849.2 and the corresponding interest in a lump sum.

After the judgment was pronounced at first instance, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory time limit, and the judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
